original: The Central Authority shall consist of a Chief Commissioner and such number of other Commissioners as may be prescribed, to be appointed by the Central Government to exercise the powers and discharge the functions under this Act.
simplification: The Central Authority is run by a Chief Commissioner and some other Commissioners chosen by the central government.

original: The Central Authority shall consist of a Chief Commissioner and such number of other Commissioners as may be prescribed, to be appointed by the Central Government to exercise the powers and discharge the functions under this Act.
simplification: The Central Authority will be made up of a Chief Commissioner and a prescribed number of other Commissioners, all appointed by the Central Government to use the powers and carry out the duties under this Act.

original: The Central Authority shall consist of a Chief Commissioner and such number of other Commissioners as may be prescribed, to be appointed by the Central Government to exercise the powers and discharge the functions under this Act.
simplification: The Central Authority will not be made up of a Chief Commissioner and a prescribed number of other Commissioners, all appointed by the Central Government to use the powers and carry out the duties under this Act.

original: No act or proceeding of the Central Authority shall be invalid merely by reason of— (a) any vacancy in, or any defect in the constitution of, the Central Authority; or (b) any defect in the appointment of a person acting as the Chief Commissioner or as a Commissioner; or (c) any irregularity in the procedure of the Central Authority not affecting the merits of the case.
simplification: The Central Authority's decisions still count even if a seat is empty or there was a small mistake in how someone was appointed.

original: No act or proceeding of the Central Authority shall be invalid merely by reason of— (a) any vacancy in, or any defect in the constitution of, the Central Authority; or (b) any defect in the appointment of a person acting as the Chief Commissioner or as a Commissioner; or (c) any irregularity in the procedure of the Central Authority not affecting the merits of the case.
simplification: No action or proceeding of the Central Authority will become invalid just because of: (a) a vacancy in, or a defect in how the Central Authority was formed; (b) a defect in the appointment of a person acting as Chief Commissioner or Commissioner; or (c) any irregularity in its procedure that does not affect the merits of the case.

original: No act or proceeding of the Central Authority shall be invalid merely by reason of— (a) any vacancy in, or any defect in the constitution of, the Central Authority; or (b) any defect in the appointment of a person acting as the Chief Commissioner or as a Commissioner; or (c) any irregularity in the procedure of the Central Authority not affecting the merits of the case.
simplification: No action or proceeding of the Central Authority will become invalid just because of: (a) a vacancy in, or a defect in how the Central Authority was formed; (b) a defect in the appointment of a person acting as Chief Commissioner or Commissioner; or (c) certain irregularity in its procedure that does not affect the merits of the case.

original: A person aggrieved by any order passed by the Central Authority under sections 20 and 21 may file an appeal to the National Commission within a period of thirty days from the date of receipt of such order.
simplification: If you don't agree with a decision of the Central Authority, you can complain to the National Commission within 30 days.

original: A person aggrieved by any order passed by the Central Authority under sections 20 and 21 may file an appeal to the National Commission within a period of thirty days from the date of receipt of such order.
simplification: A person unhappy with an order made by the Central Authority under sections 20 and 21 can appeal to the National Commission within thirty days of receiving the order.

original: A person aggrieved by any order passed by the Central Authority under sections 20 and 21 may file an appeal to the National Commission within a period of thirty days from the date of receipt of such order.
simplification: A person unhappy with an order made by the Central Authority under sections 20 and 21 can appeal to the National Commission within sixty days of receiving the order.

original: Where the District Commission does not decide the issue of admissibility of the complaint within the period so specified, it shall be deemed to have been admitted.
simplification: If the District Commission doesn't decide in time, your complaint is accepted automatically.

original: Where the District Commission does not decide the issue of admissibility of the complaint within the period so specified, it shall be deemed to have been admitted.
simplification: If the District Commission does not decide whether to admit the complaint within the set time, the complaint will be treated as admitted.

original: Where the District Commission does not decide the issue of admissibility of the complaint within the period so specified, it shall be deemed to have been admitted.
simplification: If the District Commission does decide whether to admit the complaint within the set time, the complaint will be treated as admitted.

original: Where the parties agree for settlement by mediation and give their consent in writing, the District Commission shall, within five days of receipt of such consent, refer the matter for mediation, and in such case, the provisions of Chapter V, relating to mediation, shall apply.
simplification: If both sides agree in writing to talk it out, the District Commission sends the case to mediation within 5 days.

original: Where the parties agree for settlement by mediation and give their consent in writing, the District Commission shall, within five days of receipt of such consent, refer the matter for mediation, and in such case, the provisions of Chapter V, relating to mediation, shall apply.
simplification: If the parties agree to settle by mediation and give their consent in writing, the District Commission must send the matter for mediation within five days of getting that consent. In that case, the rules on mediation in Chapter V will apply.

original: Where the parties agree for settlement by mediation and give their consent in writing, the District Commission shall, within five days of receipt of such consent, refer the matter for mediation, and in such case, the provisions of Chapter V, relating to mediation, shall apply.
simplification: If the parties agree to settle by mediation and give their consent in writing, the District Commission must send the matter for mediation within ten days of getting that consent. In that case, the rules on mediation in Chapter V will apply.

original: The State Commission shall ordinarily function at the State capital and perform its functions at such other places as the State Government may in consultation with the State Commission notify in the Official Gazette: Provided that the State Government may, by notification, establish regional benches of the State Commission, at such places, as it deems fit.
simplification: The State Commission usually works in the state capital, but it can also work in other places the government chooses.

original: The State Commission shall ordinarily function at the State capital and perform its functions at such other places as the State Government may in consultation with the State Commission notify in the Official Gazette: Provided that the State Government may, by notification, establish regional benches of the State Commission, at such places, as it deems fit.
simplification: The State Commission will usually work from the State capital. It can also work at other places that the State Government, after consulting the State Commission, announces in the Official Gazette. The State Government may also set up regional benches of the State Commission at places it thinks suitable.

original: The State Commission shall ordinarily function at the State capital and perform its functions at such other places as the State Government may in consultation with the State Commission notify in the Official Gazette: Provided that the State Government may, by notification, establish regional benches of the State Commission, at such places, as it deems fit.
simplification: The State Commission will not usually work from the State capital. It can also work at other places that the State Government, after consulting the State Commission, announces in the Official Gazette. The State Government may also set up regional benches of the State Commission at places it thinks suitable.

original: Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1), a complaint may be entertained after the period specified in sub-section (1), if the complainant satisfies the District Commission, the State Commission or the National Commission, as the case may be, that he had sufficient cause for not filing the complaint within such period: Provided that no such complaint shall be entertained unless the District Commission or the State Commission or the National Commission, as the case may be, records its reasons for condoning such delay.
simplification: If you file a consumer complaint late, it can still be accepted if you had a good reason. The commission has to write down why it is allowing it.

original: Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1), a complaint may be entertained after the period specified in sub-section (1), if the complainant satisfies the District Commission, the State Commission or the National Commission, as the case may be, that he had sufficient cause for not filing the complaint within such period: Provided that no such complaint shall be entertained unless the District Commission or the State Commission or the National Commission, as the case may be, records its reasons for condoning such delay.
simplification: Even though sub-section (1) sets a time limit, a complaint can still be accepted after that period if the complainant shows the District, State or National Commission that there was a good reason for the delay. But the Commission must write down its reasons for excusing the delay before accepting such a complaint.

original: Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1), a complaint may be entertained after the period specified in sub-section (1), if the complainant satisfies the District Commission, the State Commission or the National Commission, as the case may be, that he had sufficient cause for not filing the complaint within such period: Provided that no such complaint shall be entertained unless the District Commission or the State Commission or the National Commission, as the case may be, records its reasons for condoning such delay.
simplification: Even though sub-section (1) sets a time limit, a complaint can still be accepted after that period if the complainant shows the District, State or National Commission that there was a good reason for the delay.

original: Save as otherwise provided, the offences under sub-section (1) shall be tried summarily by the District Commission or the State Commission or the National Commission, as the case may be.
simplification: These offences are handled in a fast, simple trial by the consumer commission.

original: Save as otherwise provided, the offences under sub-section (1) shall be tried summarily by the District Commission or the State Commission or the National Commission, as the case may be.
simplification: Unless stated otherwise, the District, State or National Commission will try the offences under sub-section (1) in a summary (quick) way.

original: Save as otherwise provided, the offences under sub-section (1) shall be tried summarily by the District Commission or the State Commission or the National Commission, as the case may be.
simplification: The District, State or National Commission will try the offences under sub-section (1) in a summary (quick) way.

original: A product liability action may be brought by a complainant against a product manufacturer or a product service provider or a product seller, as the case may be, for any harm caused to him on account of a defective product.
simplification: If a broken or faulty product hurts you, you can take action against the company that made it, sold it or serviced it.

original: A product liability action may be brought by a complainant against a product manufacturer or a product service provider or a product seller, as the case may be, for any harm caused to him on account of a defective product.
simplification: A complainant can bring a product liability case against a product manufacturer, a product service provider or a product seller for any harm caused to them by a defective product.

original: A product liability action may be brought by a complainant against a product manufacturer or a product service provider or a product seller, as the case may be, for any harm caused to him on account of a defective product.
simplification: A complainant can bring a product liability case against a product manufacturer, a product service provider or a product seller for certain harm caused to them by a defective product.

original: No cognizance shall be taken by a competent court of any offence under sections 88 and 89 except on a complaint filed by the Central Authority or any officer authorised by it in this behalf.
simplification: A court will only look at these offences if the Central Authority or its officer files the complaint.

original: No cognizance shall be taken by a competent court of any offence under sections 88 and 89 except on a complaint filed by the Central Authority or any officer authorised by it in this behalf.
simplification: A competent court will not take up any offence under sections 88 and 89 unless a complaint is filed by the Central Authority or by an officer it has authorised for this purpose.

original: No cognizance shall be taken by a competent court of any offence under sections 88 and 89 except on a complaint filed by the Central Authority or any officer authorised by it in this behalf.
simplification: A competent court will not take up any offence under sections 88 and 89.

original: Any offence punishable under sections 88 and 89, may, either before or after the institution of the prosecution, be compounded, on payment of such amount as may be prescribed: Provided that no compounding of such offence shall be made without the leave of the court before which a complaint has been filed under section 92: Provided further that such sum shall not, in any case, exceed the maximum amount of the fine, which may be imposed under this Act for the offence so compounded.
simplification: Some offences can be settled by paying money instead of going through a full trial. The court has to agree, and the payment can't be more than the biggest fine allowed.

original: Any offence punishable under sections 88 and 89, may, either before or after the institution of the prosecution, be compounded, on payment of such amount as may be prescribed: Provided that no compounding of such offence shall be made without the leave of the court before which a complaint has been filed under section 92: Provided further that such sum shall not, in any case, exceed the maximum amount of the fine, which may be imposed under this Act for the offence so compounded.
simplification: Any offence punishable under sections 88 and 89 can be settled by paying a prescribed amount, either before or after the prosecution starts. However, it cannot be settled without the permission of the court where the complaint was filed under section 92. Also, the amount can never be more than the maximum fine that this Act allows for that offence.

original: Any offence punishable under sections 88 and 89, may, either before or after the institution of the prosecution, be compounded, on payment of such amount as may be prescribed: Provided that no compounding of such offence shall be made without the leave of the court before which a complaint has been filed under section 92: Provided further that such sum shall not, in any case, exceed the maximum amount of the fine, which may be imposed under this Act for the offence so compounded.
simplification: Any offence punishable under sections 88 and 178 can be settled by paying a prescribed amount, either before or after the prosecution starts. However, it cannot be settled without the permission of the court where the complaint was filed under section 92. Also, the amount can never be more than the maximum fine that this Act allows for that offence.

original: Where an offence has been compounded under sub-section (1), no proceeding or further proceeding, as the case may be, shall be taken against the offender in respect of the offence so compounded.
simplification: After an offence is settled by paying money, the person can't be taken to court again for it.

original: Where an offence has been compounded under sub-section (1), no proceeding or further proceeding, as the case may be, shall be taken against the offender in respect of the offence so compounded.
simplification: Once an offence has been settled under sub-section (1), no new or further case will be taken against the offender for that offence.

original: The general superintendence, direction and management of the affairs of the Central Information Commission shall vest in the Chief Information Commissioner who shall be assisted by the Information Commissioners and may exercise all such powers and do all such acts and things which may be exercised or done by the Central Information Commission autonomously without being subjected to directions by any other authority under this Act.
simplification: The Chief Information Commissioner is the boss of the Central Information Commission, and the other commissioners help. The Commission works on its own without anyone else telling it what to do.

original: The general superintendence, direction and management of the affairs of the Central Information Commission shall vest in the Chief Information Commissioner who shall be assisted by the Information Commissioners and may exercise all such powers and do all such acts and things which may be exercised or done by the Central Information Commission autonomously without being subjected to directions by any other authority under this Act.
simplification: The Chief Information Commissioner is in overall charge of running the Central Information Commission, with help from the Information Commissioners. The Chief Information Commissioner may use all the powers of the Commission and do everything the Commission can do, independently and without taking orders from any other authority under this Act.

original: The general superintendence, direction and management of the affairs of the Central Information Commission shall vest in the Chief Information Commissioner who shall be assisted by the Information Commissioners and may exercise all such powers and do all such acts and things which may be exercised or done by the Central Information Commission autonomously without being subjected to directions by any other authority under this Act.
simplification: The Chief Information Commissioner is in overall charge of running the Central Information Commission, with help from the Information Commissioners. The Chief Information Commissioner may use all the powers of the Commission and do everything the Commission can do, independently and without taking orders from certain other authority under this Act.

original: केन्द्रीय सूचना आयोग के कार्यों का साधारण अधीक्षण, निदेशन और प्रबंधन, मुख्य सूचना आयुक्त में निहित होगा, जिसकी सहायता सूचना आयुक्तों द्वारा की जाएगी और वह ऐसी सभी शक्तियों का प्रयोग और ऐसे सभी कार्य और बातें कर सकेगा, जिनका केन्द्रीय सूचना आयोग द्वारा स्वतंत्र रूप से इस अधिनियम के अधीन किसी अन्य प्राधिकारी के निदेशों के अधीन रहे बिना प्रयोग किया जा सकता है या जो की जा सकती है।
simplification: मुख्य सूचना आयुक्त केंद्रीय सूचना आयोग को चलाते हैं और दूसरे आयुक्त उनकी मदद करते हैं। आयोग अपने फ़ैसले खुद लेता है, कोई और उसे आदेश नहीं देता।

original: केन्द्रीय सूचना आयोग के कार्यों का साधारण अधीक्षण, निदेशन और प्रबंधन, मुख्य सूचना आयुक्त में निहित होगा, जिसकी सहायता सूचना आयुक्तों द्वारा की जाएगी और वह ऐसी सभी शक्तियों का प्रयोग और ऐसे सभी कार्य और बातें कर सकेगा, जिनका केन्द्रीय सूचना आयोग द्वारा स्वतंत्र रूप से इस अधिनियम के अधीन किसी अन्य प्राधिकारी के निदेशों के अधीन रहे बिना प्रयोग किया जा सकता है या जो की जा सकती है।
simplification: केन्द्रीय सूचना आयोग के कामकाज की देखरेख, निर्देशन और प्रबंधन मुख्य सूचना आयुक्त के पास होगा, और सूचना आयुक्त उसकी मदद करेंगे। मुख्य सूचना आयुक्त आयोग की सभी शक्तियों का इस्तेमाल कर सकेगा और वे सभी काम कर सकेगा जो आयोग स्वतंत्र रूप से, किसी दूसरे प्राधिकारी के निर्देश के बिना, इस अधिनियम के तहत कर सकता है।

original: केन्द्रीय सूचना आयोग के कार्यों का साधारण अधीक्षण, निदेशन और प्रबंधन, मुख्य सूचना आयुक्त में निहित होगा, जिसकी सहायता सूचना आयुक्तों द्वारा की जाएगी और वह ऐसी सभी शक्तियों का प्रयोग और ऐसे सभी कार्य और बातें कर सकेगा, जिनका केन्द्रीय सूचना आयोग द्वारा स्वतंत्र रूप से इस अधिनियम के अधीन किसी अन्य प्राधिकारी के निदेशों के अधीन रहे बिना प्रयोग किया जा सकता है या जो की जा सकती है।
simplification: केन्द्रीय सूचना आयोग के कामकाज की देखरेख, निर्देशन और प्रबंधन मुख्य सूचना आयुक्त के पास होगा, और सूचना आयुक्त उसकी मदद करेंगे। मुख्य सूचना आयुक्त आयोग की सभी शक्तियों का इस्तेमाल कर सकेगा और वे कुछ काम कर सकेगा जो आयोग स्वतंत्र रूप से, किसी दूसरे प्राधिकारी के निर्देश के बिना, इस अधिनियम के तहत कर सकता है।

original: The Chief Information Commissioner or an Information Commissioner shall not be a Member of Parliament or Member of the Legislature of any State or Union territory, as the case may be, or hold any other office of profit or connected with any political party or carrying on any business or pursuing any profession.
simplification: The people who run the Information Commission can't be politicians or join a political party. They also can't have another paid job or run a business.

original: The Chief Information Commissioner or an Information Commissioner shall not be a Member of Parliament or Member of the Legislature of any State or Union territory, as the case may be, or hold any other office of profit or connected with any political party or carrying on any business or pursuing any profession.
simplification: The Chief Information Commissioner or an Information Commissioner cannot be a Member of Parliament or of the legislature of any State or Union territory. They also cannot hold any other paid office, be linked to any political party, run a business or practise a profession.

original: The Chief Information Commissioner or an Information Commissioner shall not be a Member of Parliament or Member of the Legislature of any State or Union territory, as the case may be, or hold any other office of profit or connected with any political party or carrying on any business or pursuing any profession.
simplification: The Chief Information Commissioner or an Information Commissioner cannot be a Member of Parliament or of the legislature of any State or Union territory. They also cannot hold any other paid office, be linked to certain political party, run a business or practise a profession.

original: मुख्य सूचना आयुक्त या कोई सूचना आयुक्त, यथास्थिति, संसद् का सदस्य या किसी राज्य या संघ राज्यक्षेत्र के विधान-मंडल का सदस्य नहीं होगा या कोई अन्य लाभ का पद धारित नहीं करेगा या किसी राजनैतिक दल से संबद्ध नहीं होगा अथवा कोई कारबार नहीं करेगा या कोई वृत्ति नहीं करेगा।

original: मुख्य सूचना आयुक्त या कोई सूचना आयुक्त, यथास्थिति, संसद् का सदस्य या किसी राज्य या संघ राज्यक्षेत्र के विधान-मंडल का सदस्य नहीं होगा या कोई अन्य लाभ का पद धारित नहीं करेगा या किसी राजनैतिक दल से संबद्ध नहीं होगा अथवा कोई कारबार नहीं करेगा या कोई वृत्ति नहीं करेगा।

original: The Chief Information Commissioner or an Information Commissioner shall before he enters upon his office make and subscribe before the President or some other person appointed by him in that behalf, an oath or affirmation according to the form set out for the purpose in the First Schedule.
simplification: Before they start their job, the information commissioners have to make a formal promise in front of the President or someone the President chooses.

original: The Chief Information Commissioner or an Information Commissioner shall before he enters upon his office make and subscribe before the President or some other person appointed by him in that behalf, an oath or affirmation according to the form set out for the purpose in the First Schedule.
simplification: Before starting work, the Chief Information Commissioner or an Information Commissioner must take an oath or affirmation in front of the President or a person the President appoints for this. The oath must follow the form given in the First Schedule.

original: The Chief Information Commissioner or an Information Commissioner shall before he enters upon his office make and subscribe before the President or some other person appointed by him in that behalf, an oath or affirmation according to the form set out for the purpose in the First Schedule.

original: केन्द्रीय सरकार, राजपत्र में किसी अधिसूचना द्वारा, अनुसूची का उस सरकार द्वारा स्थापित किसी अन्य आसूचना या सुरक्षा संगठन को उसमें सम्मिलित करके या उसमें पहले से विनिर्दिष्ट किसी संगठन का उससे लोप करके, संशोधन कर सकेगी और ऐसी अधिसूचना के प्रकाशन पर ऐसे संगठन को अनुसूची में, यथास्थिति, सम्मिलित किया गया या उसका उससे लोप किया गया समझा जाएगा।
simplification: केंद्र सरकार ख़ुफ़िया या सुरक्षा एजेंसियों को खास सूची में जोड़ या हटा सकती है। सूचना छपते ही सूची बदल जाती है।

simplification: केन्द्रीय सरकार राजपत्र में अधिसूचना देकर अनुसूची में बदलाव कर सकती है। वह अपने बनाए किसी दूसरे आसूचना या सुरक्षा संगठन को इसमें जोड़ सकती है, या पहले से लिखे किसी संगठन को हटा सकती है। अधिसूचना छपने पर वह संगठन अनुसूची में जोड़ा गया या उससे हटाया गया माना जाएगा।
